pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 14.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: PLAY- RELATING TO REAL LIFE

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.4: Reading 14.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play- Relating to real life

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Reading 14.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play- Relating to real life
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What makes plays interesting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify the characters in a play
2. discuss the various themes in a play
3. appreciate the beauty of performance of a literary text

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Reading 14.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play- Relating to real life

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Reading 14.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play- Relating to real life

Teach
• Focus skill: identify the characters in a play.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Reading 14.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play- Relating to real life.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Reading 14.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play- Relating to real life
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What makes plays interesting?
2. Why is it important for an actor to pronounce words correctly and speak audibly in a performance?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
